## How Biome's `overrides` and ignore precedence work

**Override matching behavior:** When a file is matched against an override pattern, the configuration specified in that pattern will override the top-level configuration. The order of the patterns matter—if a file can match three patterns, only the first one is used.

**Overrides exclude ignore/include options:** In override blocks, the formatter and linter configurations behave differently from top-level settings. Overrides include the options of the top level formatter configuration, minus ignore and include, and also include the options of the top level linter configuration, minus ignore and include. This is relevant to the concept that path ignoring in overrides should be scoped only to the override's own settings.

## The historical include/ignore precedence issue

The precedence question you referenced was a known point of confusion. In Biome v1, when both include and ignore were specified, ignore took precedence over include—effectively meaning that if you had any ignore rule, your include rules were completely ignored.

The maintainers acknowledged this needed changing: they agreed the logic should change in V2—computing ignore first, and include second.

## The V2 configuration simplification (RFC)

There was a significant redesign proposed to reduce the complexity that led to these override/ignore bugs. Biome provides several ways to tune the behavior of tools for a given set of files—.gitignore files, global include/ignore, by-tool include/ignore, and granular overrides. The resulting configuration schema is pretty complex and can be confusing when these features are used together.

The resulting configuration provided multiple ways to achieve the same thing and led to numerous bugs around overriding behaviors. The proposed solution was to reduce this complexity and improve composability by getting rid of the {files,formatter,linter,organizeImports}.{include,ignore} properties.

## Current V2 `files.includes` semantics

In the current version, ignoring is handled via negated patterns in `files.includes`: to exclude files and folders from being processed by Biome, you can use the files.includes configuration with negated patterns—a leading ! to ignore files from being linted/formatted, and a double leading !! to ignore files from any project-related operation.

Importantly for precedence: files.includes applies to all of Biome's tools, meaning the files specified there are processed by the linter, the formatter and the assist, unless specified otherwise. For the individual tools, you can further refine the matching files using <tool>.includes. Also note that the global files.includes has slightly different semantics than the more specific <tool>.includes fields.
